suggestions.assertion: No $var references inside childJob variables object
suggestions.reason: In loop mode (data_array set), the skill's own spec requires variables: {} (empty) — so this assertion is largely redundant with 'childJob variables is {} (empty) when using data_array': any output satisfying the latter automatically satisfies the former, since an empty object cannot contain a $var string. It would be more discriminating as a single-mode check (workflow field set to a fixed workflow with static per-key {task,value} variables) where a $var string genuinely could sneak into variables and cause the documented indefinite-hang bug.

None of the seven expectations verify the actual semantic content that fulfills the user's request — e.g., that childJob.workflow == "Device Backup" (the specific child workflow named in the task) or that data_array points at a genuine per-device array input. A subtly wrong build (e.g., wiring the loop against the wrong workflow name, or against a static array instead of a job input) would still pass every listed expectation. Consider adding an assertion on the 'workflow' field value and/or that data_array references a job-level array variable.

No assertion checks that the child workflow itself is well-formed (always completes via try-catch, has error transitions on adapter tasks) even though this is explicitly required by the skill's Guide 4 'Building the child workflow' section and is essential for the parent's childJob loop to produce usable per-iteration taskStatus results. I verified this independently and it held, but a genuinely broken child workflow (e.g., no error transition, leaving a loop iteration stuck) would not be caught by any of the given expectations.

eval_feedback.overall: All seven expectations passed with strong, verifiable evidence — cross-checked not just against the transcript's narrative claims but independently against the real production asset files (helpers/assets/*.json) the executor said it consulted, and every cross-check confirmed the transcript's claims were accurate rather than fabricated. The assertions correctly target well-documented, high-consequence childJob gotchas (wrong actor/task/job_details/variables shape causes runtime hangs or validation failures per the skill's own Gotchas list), so a genuinely wrong build would very likely fail one or more of them. The main gap is that no expectation checks the task-specific semantics (correct child workflow name, correct data source) or the child workflow's own completeness — both of which I verified manually and found correct, but which the expectation set does not itself guard against.
